# Adjudication Task — Chapter 594

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃594화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|콰지직!
  6|
  7|섬뜩한 파육음과 함께 지금껏 수백, 수천 번도 넘게 겪었던 느낌이 손끝을 타고 전해진다. 살을 가르고 뼈를 부수는 감각.
  8|
  9|어느 순간 익숙해져 버린, 그래서 가끔은 씁쓸함을 느끼게 만드는 바로 그 감각이다.
 10|
 11|이런 것에 익숙해졌다는 뜻은 그만큼 많은 생명을 내 손으로 직접 앗았다는 뜻이니까.
 12|
 13|하지만 적어도 이번만큼은 아니었다. 죽어 가는 사내를 바라보는 내 마음에는 일말의 씁쓸함도 느껴지지 않았다.
 14|
 15|“커……헉!”
 16|
 17|바람 빠지는 소리와 함께 흘러나온 단말마. 그와 동시에 단단한 체격의 사내가 무릎을 꿇었다.
 18|
 19|쿵.
 20|
 21|한때는 섬뜩하기까지 하던 핏빛 안광은 점차 사그라지고, 전신은 눈앞에 들이닥친 죽음 앞에서 가늘게 떨리는 중이었다.
 22|
 23|아니, 어쩌면 사내. 석고준이 두려워하는 것은 죽음 그 자체가 아니라 그에게 죽음을 내린 나일지도 모르겠다.
 24|
 25|“지, 진태경.”
 26|
 27|금방이라도 꺼질 듯한 목소리와 눈빛. 그러나 동정심 따위는 들지 않았다.
 28|
 29|상대는 나와 같은 인간이 아니라 괴물이니까.
 30|
 31|오늘 나를 비롯한 평화 길드원들이 김화종을 잃은 것처럼, 이름도 모르는 수천여 명의 사람들은 사랑하는 가족과 친구를 잃어야 했다.
 32|
 33|그런 미친 짓을 벌인 대가치고는 편한 죽음을 맞이하는 것 같아 불공평하게 느껴질 정도다.
 34|
 35|“쿨럭. 이, 이렇게 죽을 수는…….”
 36|
 37|무릎을 꿇은 채 고통으로 경련하는 석고준을, 나는 서늘한 눈빛으로 내려다보았다.
 38|
 39|“죽어라. 너 같은 병신한테는 산소도 아깝다.”
 40|
 41|구구절절한 유언을 들어 줄 생각도, 남기게 해 줄 마음도 없다. 나는 놈의 가슴을 관통한 백염을 힘주어 뽑아냈다.
 42|
 43|푸화악!
 44|
 45|투명한 창날이 뽑힘과 동시에 미처 증발하지 않은 핏물들이 분수처럼 뿜어져 나온다.
 46|
 47|가슴에 주먹만 한 구멍이 뚫린 채 멍하니 나를 올려다보던 석고준의 신형이 천천히 기울었다.
 48|
 49|철벅.
 50|
 51|그것이 마지막이었다.
 52|
 53|자신의 피로 만들어진 웅덩이에 고개를 처박은 그는 눈을 부릅뜬 상태로 움직임을 멈췄다.
 54|
 55|그리고 더 이상의 숨도, 한 줌의 생기도 느껴지지 않는 괴물의 시신을 바라보던 나는 문득 깨달았다.
 56|
 57|‘끝났구나.’
 58|
 59|지난 수십 년간 이정룡에게 충성을 바친 제자이자, 세계에서도 손꼽히는 아레스 길드의 실질적인 주인이 내 손에 죽었다.
 60|
 61|두 번의 몬스터 웨이브를 인위적으로 일으켜 수천의 사상자를 발생시키고, 김화종과 이십여 명의 평화 길드원을 희생시킨 대가를 죽음으로 받아 냈다.
 62|
 63|‘이것으로…… 정말 끝난 거야.’
 64|
 65|하지만 어째서일까. 복수를 끝마쳤음에도 마음 한구석이 텅 비어 버린 듯한 기분이 드는 이유는. 마치 죽은 석고준이 아닌 내 가슴에 구멍이 뚫린 것 같았다.
 66|
 67|그건 아마도, 곁을 떠난 이들이 두 번 다시 돌아오지 못한다는 사실을 알고 있기 때문일 것이다.
 68|
 69|‘아직도 추우십니까. 여전히 어두우십니까.’
 70|
 71|나는 닿지 않을 물음을 던지며 돌아섰다.
 72|
 73|감히 상상할 수도 없을 만큼의 무게로 전신을 짓누르는 피로와 졸음을 참으며, 격전으로 초토화된 어두운 복도를 천천히 가로질렀다.
 74|
 75|저벅.
 76|
 77|걸음걸음마다 사람들의 얼굴과 어떤 기억이 떠올라 눈 앞을 가렸다.
 78|
 79|무너지는 광안대교가 보였고 공포에 찬 사람들의 비명이 들렸다. 어느 승용차의 백미러에 매달린 가족사진 속에서 아주 오래전, 한없이 그리운 누군가와 새끼손가락을 걸고 했던 약속을 떠올렸다.
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|‘하연이가 좀 더 크면, 그리고 태경이 네가 중학생이 되면 그때 다시 바다 보러 오자. 알았지?’
 84|
 85|‘진짜?’
 86|
 87|‘당연하지. 자, 약속.’
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|하지만 오늘. 마음 깊은 곳에 간직하고 있던 약속의 장소가 무너졌다.
 92|
 93|죄 없는 사람들이 죽고 몬스터가 역병처럼 창궐했다. 최선을 다했으나 더 많은 목숨을 구하지 못했다.
 94|
 95|저벅.
 96|
 97|비틀거리는 걸음만큼이나 마음 역시 어지러웠다. 그 혼란함 속에서 따뜻한 목소리가 머릿속에서 울려 퍼졌다.
 98|
 99|
100|
101|‘자네 잘못이 아니야.’
102|
103|‘……!’
104|
105|‘자네는 최선을 다했네.’
106|
107|
108|
109|죽어 가면서도 나를 위로해 주었던 반백의 노집사는 돌아올 수 없는 여정을 떠났다.
110|
111|그가 도착한 곳이 밤인지, 낮인지. 추운지, 따뜻한지 나로서는 알 길이 없었다. 다만 바랄 뿐이다.
112|
113|그 세상이 조금이라도 환하기를. 추위에 떨던 그가 더 따뜻하기를.
114|
115|그리고…… 마지막으로 만나고 싶어 했던 한 사람이 왔다는 내 거짓말을 끝까지 믿었기를.
116|
117|저벅.
118|
119|결과가 없는 과정은 없다. 누군가가 대가를 치러야 한다고 생각했다. 잘못을 저지르면 벌을 받는 것이 순리(順理)라고 믿었다.
120|
121|그래서 나는 이곳에 왔다. 누구도 범접할 수 없었던 왕궁의 문을 열어젖히고, 난공불락(難攻不落)의 철옹성을 함락시켰다.
122|
123|싸우고, 싸우고, 또 싸웠다. 그리고 마침내 인두겁을 뒤집어쓴 괴물을 죽이고 나니, 문득 가슴이 공허해지며 한 가지 의문이 들었다.
124|
125|‘이제 어떻게 해야 하지?’
126|
127|모든 일의 원흉인 석고준을 처치한다면 조금이라도 이 분노가 사라질 줄 알았다. 후련함에 크게 소리 내어 웃을 수도 있을 것 같았다.
128|
129|하지만 아니었다. 나는 단 한 번의 손짓으로 거대한 구덩이를 만들고 메울 수도 있지만, 정작 마음의 빈자리는 메우지 못했다.
130|
131|삼 년 전에도 그랬고, 지금도 마찬가지다.
132|
133|‘빌어먹을.’
134|
135|입맛이 썼다. 결국 상처를 감내하는 것은 남은 자들의 몫으로 고스란히 남았다.
136|
137|석고준에게 너무 고통 없는 죽음을 내린 것이 아닌가 하는 후회가 들 만큼…….
138|
139|저벅.
140|
141|나는 문득 발걸음을 멈췄다. 어느새 알 수 없는 위화감이 전신을 사로잡고 있었다. 서늘한 한기가 등골을 타고 스멀스멀 기어올랐다.
142|
143|‘뭐지, 이 기분은?’
144|
145|극심한 피로 때문인지. 그게 아니라면 복잡한 마음 때문인지 머릿속이 안개처럼 흐릿했다.
146|
147|하지만 잠시 후, 우뚝 선 채 생각에 잠겨 있던 나는 마침내 위화감의 정체를 깨달을 수 있었다.
148|
149|‘분명 석고준은 죽었을 텐데. 그런데 왜…….’
150|
151|왜 처치를 알리는 시스템 창은 아직까지도 뜨지 않을까.
152|
153|가슴 한복판에 창날을 박아넣고 장기를 태웠는데. 피 웅덩이에 얼굴을 처박은 채 숨이 멎는 것을 직접 보고 느꼈는데.
154|
155|“설마.”
156|
157|나는 낮게 뇌까리며 돌아섰다. 격전으로 인하여 처참히 파괴된 복도에는 유난히 짙은 어둠이 내려앉아 있었다.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|시스템은 절대적이며 즉각적이다.
166|
167|승리의 순간 찾아온 극심한 피로와 깊은 생각에 잠겨 있던 탓에 이상함을 알아차리지 못했을 뿐, 나는 그 사실을 누구보다 잘 알고 있었다.
168|
169|그렇기에 석고준이 누워 있던 피 웅덩이가 텅 빈 것을 보고도 크게 놀라지 않았다.
170|
171|‘살아 있다. 석고준이.’
172|
173|그것 하나만큼은 확실해졌다.
174|
175|다만 내가 궁금한 것은, 도대체 어떻게 그럴 수 있느냐는 것이었다.
176|
177|A구역에는 석고준과 나, 단 두 명뿐이었고 놈은 분명히 죽음을 맞이한 상태였다.
178|
179|심장이 멎고 호흡이 정지했으니, 최상급 포션으로 반신욕을 한다 해도 살아나는 건 불가능했다.
180|
181|‘그런데 어떻게?’
182|
183|나는 의문과 함께 석고준이 남긴 흔적을 쫓아 이동하기 시작했다.
184|
185|A구역은 극소수의 인원에게만 허락된 비밀 구역답게 미로 같은 구조를 지니고 있었지만, 오직 한 방향을 향해 이어진 핏물을 따라가는 것은 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다.
186|
187|나는 빠르게 공간을 가로지르며 주위의 정보를 받아들였다.
188|
189|‘조력자는 없고. 흔적을 지울 틈이나 여유도 없었어.’
190|
191|놈이 남긴 흔적에서 급박함이 느껴졌다. 홀로 바짝 엎드린 채 필사적으로 기어가는 모습이 눈앞에 스치는 듯했다. 그리고…….
192|
193|‘마침내 두 다리로 일어났다. 바로 여기에서.’
194|
195|핏물로 선명히 찍힌 두 개의 족적(足跡). 벽면에는 무수한 손자국 역시 함께 찍혀 있었다.
196|
197|도대체 뭘까. 놈은 왜 고통으로 몸부림친 걸까. 그리고 나는 얼마 지나지 않아 그 의문에 대한 답을 찾을 수 있었다.
198|
199|‘저건.’
200|
201|그것은 피였다.
202|
203|인간의 선홍빛 피가 아닌, 푸른 빛이 감도는 몬스터의 푸른 핏방울.
204|
205|이와 같은 것들이 의미하는 바는 명백하다. 손에 닿은 몬스터의 피를 말없이 바라보던 나는 신형을 날렸다.
206|
207|쉬익!
208|
209|좌우를 스치는 바람 사이로 짙은 혈향(血香)과 악취가 느껴졌다. 극심한 피로에 휩싸인 와중에도 가까워지는 누군가의 인기척을 느낄 수 있었다.
210|
211|그리고 내 발걸음이 또 다른 복도에 들어섰을 때.
212|
213|나는 마침내 두 눈으로 직접 확인할 수 있었다.
214|
215|마지막으로 봤던 모습과는 너무나도 달라진 그놈을.
216|
217|“석고준.”
218|
219|입술 사이로 흘러나온 목소리가 나직하게 울려 퍼졌다. 동시에 비틀거리며 복도를 걸어가던 석고준이, 아니 ‘괴물’이 돌아섰다.
220|
221|“크륵. 쿠룩.”
222|
223|무슨 말을 하려는지 모를 쇳소리는 다른 부분들에 비하면 아무것도 아니다.
224|
225|4m에 이르는 거체와 터질 듯 부푼 팔과 다리는 기괴했고, 종이 다른 생물을 섞어 놓은 듯 제각각의 형태와 특징을 지닌 모습은 끔찍했다.
226|
227|유일하게 본래의 형태를 유지하고 있는 것이 있다면, 그건 비늘로 반쯤 뒤덮인 인간의 얼굴과 그 사이로 빛나는 핏빛 안광이었다.
228|
229|“진……태경. 카룩.”
230|
231|두려움과 증오가 뒤섞인 눈동자가 이쪽을 향한다. 놈의 모습을 위아래로 훑은 나는 혐오를 담아 입을 열었다.
232|
233|“그렇게까지 살아남고 싶었나? 몬스터가 되면서까지?”
234|
235|“닥, 쳐라. 이건. 이건 나도 바라지 않았던-”
236|
237|콰득! 우지직!
238|
239|그건 순식간에 벌어진 일이었다.
240|
241|석고준이 말을 잇기도 전, 보이지 않는 손이 움직인 것처럼 난데없이 놈의 오른팔이 꺾이고 푸른 핏물이 터져 나왔다.
242|
243|“크아아악!”
244|
245|고통에 찬 비명. 동시에 석고준의 기괴한 몸뚱어리에서 빠른 변화가 시작되었다.
246|
247|스륵. 투두둑!
248|
249|몬스터의 그것처럼 두꺼운 가죽과 비늘로 뒤덮인 피부가 아물고, 으스러진 뼈마디가 퍼즐처럼 짜 맞춰진다.
250|
251|“헉. 허억.”
252|
253|아직 가시지 않은 고통으로 숨을 헐떡이는 석고준. 그 모습에 나는 놈이 어떻게 여기까지 왔는지 알 것 같았다.
254|
255|“트롤(Troll). 맞지?”
256|
257|“……!”
258|
259|툭 건넨 말에 놈의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨린다. 정답이라는 뜻이다.
260|
261|트롤이라면 두말할 것 없이 압도적인 회복 능력을 지닌 몬스터.

But not this time. As I looked down at the dying man, I felt no bitterness at all.

[P7]
“Kh……!”

[P8]
A final gasp escaped him like air from a punctured tire, and the solidly built man dropped to his knees.

[P9]
*Thud.*

[P10]
The blood-red glow in his eyes, once chilling to look at, slowly faded. His whole body trembled before the death closing in on him.

[P11]
No. Perhaps it wasn’t death itself that Go Jun feared. Perhaps it was me, the one who had dealt it to him.

[P12]
“J-Jin Taekyung.”

[P13]
His voice was fading, and so was the light in his eyes. I felt no pity.

[P14]
He wasn’t human like me. He was a monster.

[P15]
The Peace Guild had lost Kim Hwajong today. Thousands of people whose names I would never know had lost family and friends they loved. For the madness Go Jun had caused, this death almost seemed too easy.

[P16]
“Cough. I-I can’t die like this……”

[P17]
I looked down coldly at him as he knelt there, convulsing in pain.

[P18]
“Die. Oxygen is wasted on a piece of shit like you.”

[P19]
I had no intention of listening to a long-winded final speech, or giving him the chance to make one. I wrenched White Flame from his chest.

[P20]
*Fwoosh!*

[P21]
The moment the transparent spearhead came free, the blood that had not yet evaporated sprayed out like a fountain.

[P22]
Go Jun stared blankly up at me, a fist-sized hole in his chest. Then his body slowly tipped over.

[P23]
*Splash.*

[P24]
That was the end. His face fell into a pool of his own blood, and he stopped moving, eyes still wide open.

[P25]
As I looked at the monster’s corpse, with no breath or trace of life left in it, a thought came to me.

[P26]
*It’s over.*

[P27]
Lee Jungryong’s loyal Disciple of several decades—the man who had effectively ruled Ares Guild, one of the foremost Guilds in the world—had died by my hand.

[P28]
He had deliberately caused two Monster Waves, leaving thousands dead or injured and costing Kim Hwajong and some twenty Peace Guild members their lives. He had paid for it with his own.

[P29]
*So this really is the end…*

[P30]
Then why did I feel so hollow? I had taken my revenge, yet it felt as though the hole was in my chest, not Go Jun’s.

[P31]
Maybe it was because I knew the people who had left us would never come back.

[P32]
*Are you still cold? Is it still dark?*

[P33]
I turned away, asking questions that could never reach them.

[P34]
Fatigue and drowsiness weighed on me more heavily than I could have imagined. I fought them off and slowly crossed the dark corridor, wrecked by our battle.

[P35]
*Step.*

[P36]
With every step, faces and memories rose before my eyes.

[P37]
I saw Gwangan Bridge collapsing. I heard people screaming in terror. A family photograph dangling from a car’s rearview mirror brought back a promise I had made long ago, pinkies linked with someone I missed more than words could say.

[P38]
“When Hayeon’s a little older, and you start middle school, Taekyung, we’ll come back to see the sea. Okay?”

[P39]
“Really?”

[P40]
“Of course. Come on, pinky promise.”

[P41]
But today, the place I had kept with that promise deep in my heart had collapsed.

[P42]
Innocent people had died, and monsters had spread like a plague. I had done everything I could, but I hadn’t saved more of them.

[P43]
*Step.*

[P44]
My thoughts were as unsteady as my feet. Through the confusion, a warm voice echoed in my mind.

[P45]
“It wasn’t your fault.”

[P46]
“……!”

[P47]
“You did your best.”

[P48]
The graying old butler who had comforted me even as he died had gone somewhere he could never return from.

[P49]
I had no way of knowing whether it was night or day where he had arrived. Whether it was cold or warm. I could only hope that his world was a little brighter. That he, who had shivered in the cold, was somewhere warmer.

[P50]
And… that he had believed my lie to the very end—the lie that the person he had wanted to see one last time had come.

[P51]
*Step.*

[P52]
Every action had an outcome. Someone had to pay the price. I had believed it was only natural for a person who did wrong to be punished.

[P53]
That was why I had come here. I had thrown open the gates of a palace no one could touch and brought down an impregnable fortress.

[P54]
I had fought, and fought, and fought again. But after finally killing the monster wearing a human skin, I felt a sudden emptiness in my chest. One question came to mind.

[P55]
*What am I supposed to do now?*

[P56]
I had thought that killing Go Jun, the cause of it all, would ease my anger, even a little. I had thought I might laugh out loud with relief.

[P57]
I couldn’t.

[P58]
With one gesture, I could make a massive pit and fill it again. But I couldn’t fill the empty place in my heart.

[P59]
It had been the same three years ago. It was the same now.

[P60]
*Damn it.*

[P61]
My mouth tasted bitter. In the end, the wounds were left for those of us still here to bear.

[P62]
I almost regretted giving Go Jun such a painless death.

[P63]
*Step.*

[P64]
I stopped.

[P65]
At some point, an inexplicable sense that something was wrong had taken hold of me. A chill crept up my spine.

[P66]
*What is this feeling?*

[P67]
Was it the exhaustion? Or everything weighing on my mind? My thoughts were as murky as fog.

[P68]
I stood there for a moment. Then I realized what was wrong.

[P69]
*Go Jun should be dead. So why…*

[P70]
Why hadn’t the System window announcing the kill appeared?

[P71]
I had driven my spearhead into the center of his chest and burned his organs. I had seen his face fall into that pool of blood and felt his breathing stop.

[P72]
“Don’t tell me.”

[P73]
I muttered the words and turned around. An unusually deep darkness had settled over the ruined corridor.

[P74]
* * *

[P75]
The System was absolute, and it was immediate.

[P76]
I knew that better than anyone. Exhaustion and the thoughts that had consumed me after my apparent victory had kept me from noticing sooner.

[P77]
So when I found the pool of blood empty, I was not especially surprised.

[P78]
*He’s alive. Go Jun is alive.*

[P79]
That much was certain. What I wanted to know was how.

[P80]
There had been only two of us in Area A: Go Jun and me. He had been dead. His heart had stopped, and he had stopped breathing. Even a half-body bath in top-grade potion could not have brought him back.

[P81]
*Then how?*

[P82]
I followed the traces he had left behind.

[P83]
Area A was a maze, fitting for a secret zone open to only a handful of people. But the trail of blood led in one direction, and it was easy enough to follow.

[P84]
I moved quickly, taking in what I saw.

[P85]
*No one helped him. He didn’t have time to cover his tracks, either.*

[P86]
The marks told me he had been desperate. I could almost see him crawling alone, pressed flat against the floor, struggling to keep going.

[P87]
And then…

[P88]
*He got to his feet. Right here.*

[P89]
Two clear footprints stood out in the blood. Countless handprints marked the wall beside them.

[P90]
What had happened to him? Why had he been writhing in pain?

[P91]
Before long, I found the answer.

[P92]
*That’s…*

[P93]
Blood.

[P94]
Not the bright red of human blood. Blue drops of monster blood, faintly gleaming.

[P95]
There was no mistaking what that meant. I stared at the monster blood on my hand, then shot forward.

[P96]
*Whoosh!*

[P97]
The wind rushed past me, carrying a strong scent of blood and a foul stench. Even through my exhaustion, I could sense someone drawing closer.

[P98]
Then I entered another corridor and saw him with my own eyes.

[P99]
He looked nothing like he had the last time I saw him.

[P100]
“Go Jun.”

[P101]
My quiet voice echoed down the corridor. Go Jun—or rather, the *monster*—turned as he staggered along.

[P102]
“Krrk. Kurruk.”

[P103]
Whatever he was trying to say came out as a metallic rasp. Compared with the rest of him, that was nothing.

[P104]
He stood four meters tall. His arms and legs were grotesquely swollen, as if they might burst. His body looked like creatures of different species had been thrown together, each part bearing its own shape and features.

[P105]
Only his face had kept anything like its original form: a human face half-covered in scales, with blood-red eyes shining between them.

[P106]
“Jin… Taekyung. Karruk.”

[P107]
Fear and hatred mingled in his eyes as he looked at me. I took in the sight of him from head to toe and spoke with disgust.

[P108]
“Did you want to live that badly? Even if it meant becoming a monster?”

[P109]
“Shut… up. This… this isn’t what I wanted either—”

[P110]
*Crack! KRAK!*

[P111]
Before he could finish, his right arm suddenly bent as if an invisible hand had twisted it. Blue blood burst from the break.

[P112]
“GRAAAAH!”

[P113]
As he screamed, his grotesque body began changing rapidly.

[P114]
*Shlk. Crackle!*

[P115]
The hide- and scale-covered skin healed. Crushed bones fitted themselves back together like pieces of a puzzle.

[P116]
“Hah. Hah.”

[P117]
Go Jun panted, still in pain. Watching him, I began to understand how he had made it this far.

[P118]
“Troll. Right?”

[P119]
“……!”

[P120]
His eyelids trembled at the question. I had my answer.

[P121]
Trolls had extraordinary regenerative abilities. The Named Monster that had originally owned the S-grade Magic Gem Go Jun had absorbed must have been an immensely powerful Troll.

[P122]
And…

[P123]
*That wasn’t the only S-grade Magic Gem he absorbed.*

[P124]
One look at him was enough to tell me. His swollen body and incredible regeneration were Troll traits, but the scales and hide covering half of him had come from another monster.

[P125]
*Mutation. That’s what he’s become.*

[P126]
Unlike mana, magical power was dark and turbid. It corrupted humans. After absorbing two S-grade Magic Gems packed with it, of course the forces inside him would clash.

[P127]
“Kurruk. I could have been stronger. Stronger than this. But you. You…”

[P128]
I cut him off.

[P129]
“Not stronger. You would’ve become an even more horrifying monster. Look at yourself.”

[P130]
“……!”

[P131]
“You’re worse than a monster. You’re no Hunter, no human—just a monster. That’s what you are.”

[P132]
*Step.*

[P133]
I moved toward him. Go Jun stared at me, eyes wide, and shouted as though he were screaming.

[P134]
“Don’t come closer! Krrk! Stay away!”

[P135]
“That’s going to be hard. There’s a monster right in front of me.”

[P136]
“T-This can’t be!”

[P137]
His blood-red eyes filled with fear.

[P138]
He must have known it, too. His body was showing signs of falling apart while he stood still. There was no way he could fight me in that condition.

[P139]
*Tap-tap-tap!*

[P140]
When Go Jun turned and ran, I wasn’t surprised. I reversed my grip on White Flame’s shaft and hurled it.

[P141]
*SHWAAAAK! BOOM!*

[P142]
A streak of flame-wreathed light burst through his legs and buried itself in the ground. He screamed and thrashed, both legs gone, while flesh and bone rapidly grew from the severed ends.

[P143]
I wasn’t going to stand there and watch.

[P144]
“Go on. Regenerate. Keep doing it as long as you can.”

[P145]
*Thud!*

[P146]
Drawing up the internal energy I had left, I rushed him. I planted my foot on his back, grabbed both of his thick arms, and pulled.

[P147]
*Crack. KRAKAKAK!*

[P148]
Go Jun lost both arms after his legs, and his scream rang through the corridor.

[P149]
I didn’t blink. I kept moving.

[P150]
*Slice! Stab!*

[P151]
I pulled the spear from the ground and slashed and stabbed him again and again. I seared the wounds that tried to close with the Flame Divine Palm, then gripped the regenerating flesh and tore it away.

[P152]
Under ordinary circumstances, I would never have done anything so brutal. Now I did not hesitate.

[P153]
*KRAKAKAK!*

[P154]
Regeneration. Destruction. Again and again.

[P155]
Go Jun was the first to give out under the endless pain.

[P156]
“GRAAAAH! S-Stop!”

[P157]
His voice was hoarse, and his eyes were not as red as before. His regeneration had been slowing for some time. Now it had stopped altogether.

[P158]
“Th-then kill me…”

[P159]
“I was going to.”

[P160]
This time, I would make sure he could never come back.

[P161]
I looked into his eyes.

[P162]
“Whether you’re going to heaven or hell, go on ahead and wait for me. When I get there, I’ll kill you to my heart’s content.”

[P163]
“……!”

[P164]
Those were the last words Go Jun heard in this world.

[P165]
*It ends now.*

[P166]
I did not wait for an answer. Without a moment’s hesitation, I brought the transparent spearhead down.

[P167]
*Slice! Thud!*

[P168]
His head came free with a sharp cutting sound and rolled across the floor.

[P169]
That was the end of a monster who had become neither a hero like Cheon Taemin nor an ambitious warlord like his Master, Lee Jungryong.

[P170]
*Ding.*

[P171]
The familiar chime rang in my ears. I picked up Go Jun’s head from the pool of blood and crossed the space where I alone remained, my steps slow and unsteady.

[P172]
I was tired.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

[P126]

[P127]

[P128]
I cut him off.

[P129]
“Not stronger. You would’ve become an even more horrifying monster. Look at yourself.”

[P130]
“……!”

[P131]

[P132]
*Step.*

[P133]

[P134]
“Don’t come closer! Krrk! Stay away!”

[P135]

[P136]
“T-This can’t be!”

[P137]
His blood-red eyes filled with fear.

[P138]

[P139]
*Tap-tap-tap!*

[P140]

[P141]
*SHWAAAAK! BOOM!*

[P142]

[P143]
I wasn’t going to stand there and watch.

[P144]

[P145]
*Thud!*

[P146]

[P147]
*Crack. KRAKAKAK!*

[P148]

[P149]
I didn’t blink. I kept moving.

[P150]
*Slice! Stab!*

[P151]

[P152]
Under ordinary circumstances, I would never have done anything so brutal. Now I did not hesitate.

[P153]
*KRAKAKAK!*

[P154]

[P155]
Go Jun was the first to give out under the endless pain.

[P156]
“GRAAAAH! S-Stop!”

[P157]

[P158]

[P159]
“I was going to.”

[P160]

[P161]
I looked into his eyes.

[P162]
“Whether you’re going to heaven or hell, go on ahead and wait for me. When I get there, I’ll kill you to my heart’s content.”

[P163]
“……!”

[P164]

[P165]
*It ends now.*

[P166]
I did not wait for an answer. Without a moment’s hesitation, I brought the transparent spearhead down.

[P167]
*Slice! Thud!*

[P168]

[P169]

[P170]
*Ding.*

[P171]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
